segments.text: We can now read equations and form them. Time to solve. And the honest truth first: there is no magic trick that cracks every differential equation. We keep a toolbox, and the first job on any equation is always diagnosis. What type is this?
The first and friendliest type: variables separable. It applies whenever the rate of change splits cleanly into an x part times a y part, d y by d x equals something in x, times something in y.
Here is the whole method in one picture: the mixed equation at the top, sorted into two baskets below.
Physically move every y, along with its d y, to the left side, and every x, along with d x, to the right, like sorting mixed laundry into two baskets. Then integrate each side entirely on its own.

If a picture helps, think of splitting a shared auto fare. As long as your expenses and your friend's expenses never get tangled together, each of you just totals up your own column. Separation works the moment the x costs and the y costs do not mix.
One warning deserves red ink before we go further. To separate, you usually divide both sides by some h of y, and that division silently assumes h of y is not zero.

But the constant function where h of y equals zero is often also a perfectly good solution of the original equation, and your division just threw it away. These lost singular solutions must be checked for and restored at the end. It is a favourite examiner trick.
That caution aside, the promise of this method is beautiful: if the variables separate, two ordinary integrals from Chapter seven finish the job. All the difficulty is in the integration itself.

Equations पढ़ना और form करना आ गया। अब solve करने की बारी। और पहले सच्ची बात: कोई magic trick नहीं है जो हर differential equation को crack कर दे। हम एक toolbox रखते हैं, और किसी भी equation पर पहला काम हमेशा diagnosis है। यह किस type की है?

पहला और सबसे friendly type: variables separable. यह तब लागू होता है जब rate of change साफ़ साफ़ split हो जाए, एक x वाला part times एक y वाला part, यानी d y by d x equals something in x, times something in y.
पूरा method एक picture में: ऊपर mixed equation, नीचे दो baskets में sorted.
हर y को, उसके d y समेत, left side ले जाइए, और हर x को, d x समेत, right side, जैसे mixed laundry दो baskets में sort की जाती है। फिर हर side को बिलकुल अलग अलग integrate कीजिए।

Picture से मदद मिलती हो तो shared auto का किराया बाँटना सोचिए। जब तक आपके ख़र्चे और आपके दोस्त के ख़र्चे आपस में उलझते नहीं, हर कोई बस अपना column total करता है। Separation उसी moment काम करता है जब x के costs और y के costs mix नहीं होते।
आगे बढ़ने से पहले एक warning लाल स्याही में। Separate करने के लिए usually दोनों sides को किसी h of y से divide करते हैं, और वह division चुपचाप मान लेता है कि h of y zero नहीं है।

लेकिन वह constant function जहाँ h of y equals zero होता है, अक्सर original equation का बिलकुल valid solution भी होता है, और आपके division ने उसे फेंक दिया। इन lost singular solutions को end में check करके restore करना ज़रूरी है। यह examiners की favourite trick है।
इस caution के बाद इस method का promise बहुत सुंदर है: variables separate हो गए, तो Chapter seven वाले दो ordinary integrals काम ख़त्म कर देते हैं। सारी difficulty सिर्फ integration में है।

sections.title: Switch to ratios: the homogeneous idea

board_events.text: When x and y refuse to separate
This won't separate — but the RHS doesn't care about the SIZES of $x$ and $y$, only their RATIO $y/x$. Divide top and bottom by $x^2$ to see it.
Homogeneous DE: the RHS is a function of $v = y/x$ alone — equivalently, homogeneous of degree ZERO: $F(\lambda x, \lambda y) = F(x,y)$.
Scale-invariance is the signature you hunt for. Fast proxy: in $M\,dx + N\,dy = 0$, homogeneous iff $M$ and $N$ have the SAME degree.
The substitution $y = vx$ forces the unknown to wear the ratio explicitly — and untangles the equation back into a separable one.
$\frac{x+y}{x-y}$ is homogeneous; $\frac{x+y+1}{x-y}$ is NOT — the lone $+1$ breaks scale-invariance. Those need an origin shift, not $y = vx$.
When $x$ is the heavier variable, the mirror substitution $x = vy$ is cleaner.

segments.text: Many equations refuse to separate, because x and y are knotted together. The second tool handles a huge class of these.
Look at this equation: d y by d x equals x squared plus y squared, over two x y. Try to sort it into baskets and you will fail, the variables are genuinely tangled.

But look closer. Divide the top and the bottom by x squared, and the right hand side becomes one plus y over x squared, over two times y over x. It does not care about the sizes of x and y at all, only about their ratio.

The definition: a first order equation is homogeneous when its right hand side is a function of v equals y over x alone; equivalently, homogeneous of degree zero, scale x and y by the same lambda and the expression is unchanged.

Scale invariance is the signature you hunt for. And here is a fast proxy for the differential form: if the equation is written as M d x plus N d y equals zero, it is homogeneous exactly when M and N are homogeneous of the same degree.

Once diagnosed, the cure is y equals v x: it forces the unknown to wear the ratio explicitly and untangles the equation back into a separable one. Homogeneous problems are really recognise, substitute, then separate.

One red flag: x plus y over x minus y is homogeneous, but x plus y plus one, over x minus y, is not, that lone plus one breaks scale invariance. Forcing y equals v x there produces nonsense; those need an origin shift, coming in a worked example.
And a small elegance saver: when x is the heavier, messier variable, the mirror substitution x equals v y runs the same logic with less algebra.
कई equations separate होने से इनकार कर देती हैं, क्योंकि x और y आपस में गुँथे होते हैं। दूसरा tool इनकी एक बड़ी class सँभालता है।
यह equation देखिए: d y by d x equals x squared plus y squared, over two x y. Baskets में sort करने की कोशिश कीजिए, नहीं होगा, variables सचमुच उलझे हैं।

लेकिन ग़ौर से देखिए। ऊपर और नीचे x squared से divide कीजिए, right hand side बन जाती है one plus y over x का square, over two times y over x. उसे x और y के sizes की परवाह ही नहीं, सिर्फ उनके ratio की है।

Definition: first order equation homogeneous है जब right hand side सिर्फ v equals y over x का function हो; equivalently, degree zero की homogeneous, x और y को same lambda से scale कीजिए और expression unchanged.

Scale invariance ही वह signature है जिसे आप ढूँढते हैं। और differential form के लिए एक fast proxy: equation M d x plus N d y equals zero लिखी हो, तो वह homogeneous exactly तब है जब M और N same degree की homogeneous हों।

Diagnosis हो गई, तो इलाज है y equals v x: यह unknown को ratio explicitly पहनाती है और equation को वापस separable में खोल देती है। Homogeneous problems असल में हैं: पहचानो, substitute करो, फिर separate करो।

एक red flag: x plus y over x minus y homogeneous है, लेकिन x plus y plus one, over x minus y, नहीं, वह अकेला plus one scale invariance तोड़ देता है। वहाँ y equals v x थोपने से nonsense; उन्हें origin shift चाहिए, जो एक worked example में आ रहा है।
और एक छोटा elegance saver: जब x ज़्यादा भारी, messy variable हो, तो mirror substitution x equals v y वही logic कम algebra में चला देती है।

sections.title: The two procedures, with their danger steps

board_events.text: Procedure A — separable, five steps
1. SEPARATE into $\frac{dy}{h(y)} = g(x)\,dx$. 2. FLAG the danger: note every value making $h(y) = 0$ — possible singular solutions you are about to lose.
3. INTEGRATE both sides, adding a SINGLE constant $C$. 4. SIMPLIFY (combine logs, exponentiate); apply any initial condition. 5. RESTORE flagged solutions that genuinely satisfy the original.
Why one constant: the two integrals each carry one, but their difference is just one new arbitrary constant. Writing two is redundant.
Procedure B — homogeneous, five steps
1. CONFIRM the type (scale test / same-degree $M, N$). 2. REWRITE the RHS as $\phi(v)$, $v = y/x$. 3. SUBSTITUTE $y = vx$, $\frac{dy}{dx} = v + x\frac{dv}{dx}$.
4. Solve the separable equation in $v$ and $x$. 5. BACK-SUBSTITUTE $v = y/x$. An answer left in $v$ scores ZERO.

segments.text: Both methods now become drills. Here they are as numbered procedures, with the danger steps built in where students bleed marks.

Procedure A, separable. One, separate: manipulate into d y over h of y equals g of x d x, y content left, x content right. Two, flag the danger before dividing: note every value making h of y zero, possible singular solutions you are about to lose.

Three, integrate both sides, adding a single arbitrary constant C. Four, simplify, combine logs, exponentiate where helpful, and if an initial condition is given, solve for C. Five, return to your flags and restore any lost solution that genuinely satisfies the original equation.

Why only one constant in step three: each indefinite integral carries its own constant, but their difference is just one new arbitrary constant. Writing two is redundant and a common source of confusion. Combine them immediately.
Procedure B, homogeneous, also five steps, and the first is the one people skip at their peril.

One, confirm the type by the scale test or the same degree check on M and N; a stray constant breaking homogeneity means stop. Two, rewrite the right hand side as phi of v. Three, substitute y equals v x, so d y by d x becomes v plus x d v by d x.
The equation collapses to the board: d v over phi of v minus v, equals d x over x. That right hand side is pure x, the substitution has manufactured a separable equation.

Four, solve that separable equation in v and x. Five, back substitute v equals y over x to return to the original variables. This last step is not decoration: an answer left in v scores zero. Came in as y, must leave as y.
अब दोनों methods drills बन जाते हैं। यह रहीं numbered procedures, उन danger steps के साथ जहाँ students के marks बहते हैं।

Procedure A, separable. One, separate: equation को d y over h of y equals g of x d x में लाइए, y content left, x content right. Two, divide से पहले danger flag कीजिए: हर वह value note कीजिए जो h of y को zero बनाती है, possible singular solutions जो खोने वाले हैं।

Three, दोनों sides integrate कीजिए, एक single arbitrary constant C जोड़ते हुए। Four, simplify कीजिए, logs combine कीजिए, जहाँ मदद मिले exponentiate कीजिए, और initial condition दी हो तो C solve कीजिए। Five, अपने flags पर लौटिए और हर वह lost solution restore कीजिए जो original equation को सचमुच satisfy करता है।

Step three में सिर्फ एक constant क्यों: हर indefinite integral अपना constant लाता है, लेकिन उनका difference बस एक नया arbitrary constant है। दो लिखना redundant है और confusion का common source. तुरंत combine कीजिए।
Procedure B, homogeneous, भी पाँच steps, और पहला वही है जिसे skip करना ख़तरनाक है।

One, type confirm कीजिए, scale test या same degree check से; stray constant homogeneity तोड़े तो रुकिए। Two, right hand side को phi of v लिखिए। Three, y equals v x substitute कीजिए, तो d y by d x बनता है v plus x d v by d x.
Equation board वाली बन जाती है: d v over phi of v minus v, equals d x over x. वह right hand side pure x है, substitution ने separable equation manufacture कर दी।

Four, उस separable equation को v और x में solve कीजिए। Five, back substitute कीजिए v equals y over x, original variables में लौटने के लिए। यह आख़िरी step सजावट नहीं है: v में छोड़ा गया answer zero score करता है। y बनकर आए थे, y बनकर ही जाना है।

sections.title: The two method templates

board_events.text: Templates to write from memory
Mirror: when $x$ dominates, put $x = vy$ and run the same reduction with roles swapped.
Integral shortcut worth marks: numerator ∝ derivative of denominator ⇒ the integral is a single logarithm — no partial fractions.
Both templates end in Chapter-7 integration. Diagnosis is the new skill; integration is the old one.

segments.text: Freeze both methods into templates you can write from memory. These four lines are the working capital of the whole chapter.

Template one, separable. The type test and the sort in one line: d y by d x equals g of x times h of y, if and only if d y over h of y equals g of x d x. If you cannot reach the right hand form, the equation is not separable.
Its solution is the pair of integrals: integral of d y over h of y equals integral of g of x d x, plus one constant C.

Template two, homogeneous. The type in two equivalent statements: the right hand side is a function phi of y over x alone, or equivalently, F of lambda x lambda y equals lambda to the zero times F of x y, perfect scale invariance.
And its reduction: put y equals v x, so d y by d x equals v plus x d v by d x, and the equation rearranges to d v over phi of v minus v, equals d x over x. Separable, guaranteed.
The mirror template: when x is the dominant, messier variable, put x equals v y instead and run the same reduction with the roles of x and y swapped. Same logic, less algebra.

Now a shortcut worth real marks. Inside any separation integral, scan whether the numerator is proportional to the derivative of the denominator. If yes, the integral is a single logarithm, log of the denominator, and you skip partial fractions entirely. You will see it save two minutes in the next worked example.
Notice where both templates end: in Chapter seven integration. Diagnosis is the only new skill here; the integration muscle you already have.
दोनों methods को templates में freeze कर लीजिए जो memory से लिखे जा सकें। यही चार lines पूरे chapter की working capital हैं।

Template one, separable. Type test और sorting एक ही line में: d y by d x equals g of x times h of y, if and only if d y over h of y equals g of x d x. Right hand वाली form तक न पहुँच पाएँ, तो equation separable नहीं है।
उसका solution integrals का pair है: integral of d y over h of y equals integral of g of x d x, plus एक constant C.

Template two, homogeneous. Type दो equivalent statements में: right hand side सिर्फ y over x का function phi है, या equivalently, F of lambda x lambda y equals lambda to the zero times F of x y, perfect scale invariance.
और उसकी reduction: y equals v x रखिए, तो d y by d x equals v plus x d v by d x, और equation rearrange होकर बनती है d v over phi of v minus v, equals d x over x. Separable, guaranteed.
Mirror template: जब x dominant, messy variable हो, तो x equals v y रखिए और वही reduction x और y के roles बदलकर चलाइए। Same logic, कम algebra.

अब एक shortcut जो असली marks दिलाता है। किसी भी separation integral के अंदर scan कीजिए कि numerator, denominator के derivative का proportional तो नहीं। है, तो integral एक single logarithm है, log of the denominator, और partial fractions पूरी तरह skip. अगले worked example में यह two minutes बचाता दिखेगा।
ध्यान दीजिए दोनों templates कहाँ ख़त्म होते हैं: Chapter seven की integration पर। नई skill सिर्फ diagnosis है; integration की muscle आपके पास पहले से है।

sections.title: Separable warm-up, then the log shortcut

board_events.text: Example 1 — CBSE: clean separation
Example 2 — JEE Main: homogeneous + shortcut
Spot it: $\frac{d}{dv}(1 - 2v - v^2) = -2(1 + v)$ — numerator ∝ derivative of denominator ⇒ instant log, NO partial fractions.
Trap: reflex partial fractions burn two minutes. Scan for the derivative pattern FIRST.

segments.text: Two solves now, one from each method. Example one, C B S E level: solve d y by d x equals four x cubed plus two, times e to the minus y.

Separate by multiplying across by e to the y: e to the y d y equals four x cubed plus two, d x. Note the danger check: e to the minus y is never zero, so no solution can be lost here. Integrate both sides.

The general solution: e to the y equals x to the fourth plus two x plus C, or taking logs, y equals log of that expression. Show the separation step explicitly and carry exactly one constant, examiners look for both.
Example two is homogeneous with a beautiful shortcut inside. Solve d y by d x equals x minus y, over x plus y.
Numerator and denominator are both degree one, ratio degree zero: homogeneous. Substitute y equals v x and separate: one plus v, over one minus two v minus v squared, d v, equals d x over x.

The moment that separates fast from slow: the derivative of the denominator is minus two minus two v, minus two times one plus v, exactly proportional to the numerator. This integral is an instant logarithm, no partial fractions needed.

Integrating: minus half log of the absolute value of one minus two v minus v squared, equals log x plus C. Exponentiate, restore v equals y over x, multiply through by x squared, and the family lands as x squared minus two x y minus y squared equals C.
The trap, named: students reflexively split into partial fractions and burn two minutes on a one line integral. Train the scan: numerator proportional to derivative of denominator, first, every time.
अब दो solves, हर method से एक। Example one, C B S E level: solve कीजिए d y by d x equals four x cubed plus two, times e to the minus y.

e to the y से multiply करके separate कीजिए: e to the y d y equals four x cubed plus two, d x. Danger check note कीजिए: e to the minus y कभी zero नहीं होता, तो यहाँ कोई solution lost नहीं हो सकता। दोनों sides integrate कीजिए।

General solution: e to the y equals x to the fourth plus two x plus C, या log लेकर, y equals log of वही expression. Separation step explicitly दिखाइए और exactly एक constant carry कीजिए, examiner दोनों देखते हैं।
Example two homogeneous है, अंदर एक ख़ूबसूरत shortcut के साथ। Solve कीजिए d y by d x equals x minus y, over x plus y.
Numerator और denominator दोनों degree one, ratio degree zero: homogeneous. y equals v x substitute करके separate कीजिए: one plus v, over one minus two v minus v squared, d v, equals d x over x.

वह moment जो fast को slow से अलग करता है: denominator का derivative है minus two minus two v, यानी minus two times one plus v, बिलकुल numerator का proportional. यह integral instant logarithm है, partial fractions की ज़रूरत नहीं।

Integrate करने पर: minus half log of one minus two v minus v squared का absolute value, equals log x plus C. Exponentiate कीजिए, v equals y over x restore कीजिए, x squared से multiply कीजिए, और family बनती है x squared minus two x y minus y squared equals C.

Trap, नाम लेकर: students reflex में partial fractions तोड़ते हैं और one line के integral पर two minutes जला देते हैं। Scan की आदत डालिए: numerator proportional to derivative of denominator, पहले, हर बार।

sections.title: A curve through a point: homogeneous with a trig integral

board_events.text: Example 3 — JEE Main: three skills in one
A curve passes through $(1, \pi/6)$ and its slope satisfies the equation below. Find the curve.

board_events.latex: y = vx:\;\; v + x\frac{dv}{dx} = v + \tan v \;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \cot v\,dv = \frac{dx}{x}

board_events.text: Back-substitute $v = y/x$: $\sin(y/x) = Cx$. Apply $(1, \pi/6)$: $\sin(\pi/6) = C$ ⇒ $C = 1/2$.
Three separate skills: diagnose homogeneity, recall $\int \cot v \, dv = \log|\sin v|$, pin $C$ with the point.

segments.text: Example three is J E E Main's favourite packaging: an initial value problem wrapped around a homogeneous equation, with a trig integral hiding inside.
The setup: a curve passes through the point one comma pi by six, and at every point its slope satisfies the equation on the board. Find the curve.
Diagnose first. The right hand side is y over x plus tan of y over x, a pure function of the ratio. Homogeneous, no doubt about it.

Substitute y equals v x. The left becomes v plus x d v by d x; the right is v plus tan v. The v on each side cancels, leaving x d v by d x equals tan v, which separates into cot v d v equals d x over x.

Integrating needs one recall from Chapter seven: the integral of cot v is log of sine v. So log sine v equals log x plus log C, and combining the logs, sine v equals C x. Writing the constant as log C is what lets the logs merge so cleanly.

Back substitute v equals y over x: sine of y over x equals C x. Now pin the constant with the given point. At x equals one, y equals pi by six: sine of pi by six equals C times one, so C equals one half.
The curve, final and boxed: sine of y over x equals x over two.

Why this counts as multi concept: you diagnosed homogeneity, recalled a non obvious trig antiderivative, and pinned the constant with an initial condition. Three separate skills, one question, and every one of them individually cheap.
Example three J E E Main की favourite packaging है: homogeneous equation के चारों ओर लिपटा initial value problem, अंदर छिपे एक trig integral के साथ।
Setup: एक curve point one comma pi by six से गुज़रता है, और हर point पर उसका slope board वाली equation को satisfy करता है। Curve निकालिए।
पहले diagnose. Right hand side है y over x plus tan of y over x, ratio का pure function. Homogeneous, कोई शक नहीं।

y equals v x substitute कीजिए। Left बनता है v plus x d v by d x; right है v plus tan v. दोनों तरफ़ का v cancel, बचता है x d v by d x equals tan v, जो separate होकर बनता है cot v d v equals d x over x.

Integration के लिए Chapter seven की एक recall चाहिए: cot v का integral है log of sine v. तो log sine v equals log x plus log C, और logs combine करके, sine v equals C x. Constant को log C लिखना ही वह चाल है जिससे logs इतनी सफ़ाई से merge होते हैं।

Back substitute कीजिए v equals y over x: sine of y over x equals C x. अब दिए हुए point से constant pin कीजिए। x equals one पर, y equals pi by six: sine of pi by six equals C times one, तो C equals one half.
Curve, final और boxed: sine of y over x equals x over two.

यह multi concept इसलिए है: आपने homogeneity diagnose की, एक non obvious trig antiderivative recall किया, और initial condition से constant pin किया। तीन अलग skills, एक question, और हर एक अकेले में आसान।

sections.title: Origin shift: when a stray constant blocks the ratio trick

board_events.text: Example 4 — JEE Advanced: reducible to homogeneous
The $+3$ and $-1$ break homogeneity — $y = vx$ fails. FIX: shift the origin to where BOTH lines vanish.

board_events.latex: \frac{dY}{dX} = \frac{X - Y}{X + Y} \;\;\text{(Example 2, in capitals!)} \;\Rightarrow\; X^2 - 2XY - Y^2 = C

board_events.text: Works only when the two lines INTERSECT. Parallel lines (proportional coefficients) ⇒ substitute $t = x + y$ instead → separable.
Origin-shift reducibility is a JEE extension beyond the strict NCERT core.

segments.text: The final worked example of this part is J E E Advanced territory: an equation that is almost homogeneous, and the surgical fix that makes it so.
Solve d y by d x equals x minus y plus three, over x plus y minus one.

Run the scale test and it fails: the lone plus three and minus one break homogeneity, so y equals v x will not work directly. But those constants are the only obstruction, and there is a fix: shift the origin to the point where both lines vanish, killing the constants.
Solve the two lines simultaneously: adding gives x equals minus one, then y equals two. Define capital X equals x plus one, capital Y equals y minus two; the differentials are unchanged.

Substituting, the numerator becomes X minus Y, the denominator X plus Y, and the equation reads d Y by d X equals X minus Y over X plus Y. <chuckle>Look familiar? It is exactly Example two, wearing capital letters.</chuckle> Borrowing that finished result: X squared minus two X Y minus Y squared equals C.
Restore the shift, X equals x plus one and Y equals y minus two, and the final answer is: x plus one squared, minus two times x plus one times y minus two, minus y minus two squared, equals C.

One structural warning: this origin shift works only when the two lines intersect. If they were parallel, coefficients proportional, you would instead substitute t equals x plus y, the common linear combination, and the equation reduces to separable. Keep that sub case in your back pocket.
And for honest bookkeeping: origin shift reducibility is a J E E extension beyond the strict N C E R T core. Boards will not demand it; J E E Advanced happily will.
इस part का आख़िरी worked example J E E Advanced की ज़मीन है: एक equation जो almost homogeneous है, और वह surgical fix जो उसे बना देता है।
Solve कीजिए d y by d x equals x minus y plus three, over x plus y minus one.

Scale test चलाइए, fail होता है: अकेले plus three और minus one homogeneity तोड़ते हैं, तो y equals v x directly काम नहीं करेगा। लेकिन रुकावट सिर्फ यही constants हैं, और fix मौजूद है: origin को उस point पर shift कीजिए जहाँ दोनों lines vanish होती हैं, constants वहीं मर जाते हैं।
दोनों lines को simultaneously solve कीजिए: जोड़ने पर x equals minus one, फिर y equals two. Define कीजिए capital X equals x plus one, capital Y equals y minus two; differentials unchanged हैं।

Substitute करने पर numerator बनता है X minus Y, denominator X plus Y, और equation पढ़ी जाती है d Y by d X equals X minus Y over X plus Y. <chuckle>जाना पहचाना लगा? यह exactly Example two है, capital letters पहनकर।</chuckle> उसका finished result उधार लीजिए: X squared minus two X Y minus Y squared equals C.
Shift restore कीजिए, X equals x plus one और Y equals y minus two, और final answer है: x plus one का square, minus two times x plus one times y minus two, minus y minus two का square, equals C.

एक structural warning: यह origin shift तभी काम करता है जब दोनों lines intersect करें। Parallel होतीं, coefficients proportional, तो बजाय इसके t equals x plus y substitute करते, common linear combination, और equation separable बन जाती। यह sub case अपनी back pocket में रखिए।
और ईमानदार bookkeeping के लिए: origin shift reducibility strict N C E R T core से आगे की J E E extension है। Boards इसे नहीं माँगेंगे; J E E Advanced ख़ुशी ख़ुशी माँगेगा।

sections.title: Pitfalls: lost solutions, forced substitutions, leftover v

board_events.text: Four leaks in solving
Losing the constant solution: dividing by $h(y)$ can erase a valid solution $h(y) = 0$. Note it BEFORE dividing; check it at the end.
Forcing $y = vx$ onto a non-homogeneous equation: a stray constant means it isn't homogeneous — shift the origin (or use a linear substitution) instead.
Leaving the answer in $v$: after solving in $v$ and $x$, back-substitute $v = y/x$. An answer containing $v$ scores zero.
Double constants / messy logs: carry exactly ONE arbitrary constant, and write log-constants as $\log C$ so they combine cleanly.
The pro reflex
Diagnosis first: do the variables separate as-is? If not, is the RHS a pure function of $y/x$? Then — inside any integral — scan for numerator ∝ derivative of denominator.
Memory hooks: separate the laundry, integrate each basket; if it only sees the ratio, let $y = vx$; divide and you might lose a root; came in as $y$, must leave as $y$.

segments.text: Before the toolbox grows again in Part two, seal the four leaks that drain marks from separable and homogeneous problems.

Leak one: losing the constant solution. Dividing by h of y to separate can erase the perfectly valid solution where h of y equals zero. Note the danger before dividing, and check the candidate at the end. Examiners love asking exactly which solution was lost.

Leak two: forcing y equals v x onto an equation that is not homogeneous. One stray constant in the numerator or denominator kills the type. The cure there is the origin shift, or a linear substitution, never brute force.
Leak three: leaving the answer in v. After solving in v and x, back substitution to v equals y over x is mandatory. An answer containing v scores zero, no matter how correct the calculus inside was.

Leak four: constant hygiene. Carry exactly one arbitrary constant, and when logs appear, write the constant as log C so everything combines into a single clean logarithm. Two floating constants and mismatched logs are where sign errors breed.
Now the reflex that organises every solve.

Diagnosis before algebra. Ask in order: do the variables separate as the equation stands? If not, is the right hand side a pure function of y over x? And once you are inside any integral, scan whether the numerator is proportional to the derivative of the denominator, the single log shortcut. <whisper>That one scan is the quiet difference between finishing the paper and not.</whisper>
Four memory hooks to close: separate the laundry, integrate each basket. If it only sees the ratio, let y equal v x. Divide and you might lose a root. And, came in as y, must leave as y.
Part two में toolbox और बढ़े, उससे पहले वे चार leaks seal कर लीजिए जो separable और homogeneous problems से marks बहा ले जाते हैं।

Leak one: constant solution खो देना। Separate करने के लिए h of y से divide करना उस बिलकुल valid solution को मिटा सकता है जहाँ h of y equals zero. Divide करने से पहले danger note कीजिए, और end में candidate check कीजिए। Examiners को यही पूछना पसंद है कि कौन सा solution lost हुआ।

Leak two: non homogeneous equation पर y equals v x थोपना। Numerator या denominator में एक stray constant type को ख़त्म कर देता है। वहाँ इलाज है origin shift, या कोई linear substitution, कभी brute force नहीं।
Leak three: answer को v में छोड़ देना। v और x में solve करने के बाद back substitution, v equals y over x, mandatory है। v वाला answer zero score करता है, अंदर की calculus चाहे कितनी सही हो।

Leak four: constant hygiene. Exactly एक arbitrary constant carry कीजिए, और logs आएँ तो constant को log C लिखिए ताकि सब कुछ एक clean logarithm में combine हो। दो तैरते constants और बेमेल logs, यहीं sign errors पनपते हैं।
अब वह reflex जो हर solve को organise करता है।

Algebra से पहले diagnosis. क्रम से पूछिए: जैसी equation है, क्या variables separate होते हैं? नहीं, तो क्या right hand side सिर्फ y over x का function है? और किसी भी integral के अंदर घुसते ही scan कीजिए कि numerator, denominator के derivative का proportional तो नहीं, single log shortcut. <whisper>यही एक scan paper पूरा होने और न होने का ख़ामोश फ़र्क़ है।</whisper>
बंद करने के लिए चार memory hooks: laundry अलग करो, हर basket को integrate करो। सिर्फ ratio दिखे, तो y equals v x. Divide किया तो root खो सकते हो। और, y बनकर आए थे, y बनकर ही जाना है।
